title: The Interview
text: One opening at {workplace}. {rival} is in the waiting room too, in a better outfit, reading your CV over your shoulder.

choices.label: Be honest: zero experience, lots of enthusiasm

ok.text: They hire you for your “raw potential”, which means less money.

effects.remember: Got your first job by being honest. Nobody believed it either.

fail.text: They hire {rival}. {Rival.he} waves on the way out. With both hands.

ok.text: Hired! Your boss mentions the Shanghai client “calls in a couple of years”.

reveal.text: The Shanghai client finally calls. You say “ni hao” and then nothing, for forty seconds. You're fired by lunch.

effects.remember: Lied about speaking Mandarin to get your first job.

blabber.text: Hired! On the way out you tell the receptionist you don't actually speak Mandarin. She says she won't tell anyone. She tells everyone.

fail.text: The interviewer answers in Mandarin. You nod for eleven minutes. No job.

choices.label: Tell the receptionist {rival}'s car is being towed

ok.text: {rival} sprints out. You get the job. {Rival.his} car was fine.

reveal.text: {rival} finds the receipt from the fake tow company. {Rival.he} tells the whole town. With slides.

effects.remember: Sent {rival} to chase a fake tow truck and took {rival.his} job.

fail.text: {rival} smiles. “Nice try.” {Rival.he} gets the job and memorises your face.

effects.remember: Tried to trick {rival} out of an interview. {Rival.he} noticed.

choices.label: Interview the interviewer for the Gazette's “Local Bosses” column

ok.text: They love talking about themselves for forty minutes. They hire you out of gratitude.

effects.remember: Got hired by interviewing your own interviewer.

choices.label: Point out that you already know every price in Kwik Mart by heart

ok.text: They test you. Tuna, 1.79. Toilet roll, 4.20. Your mum's favourite biscuits, 0.99. Hired on the spot.

effects.remember: Got the job by reciting prices like poetry.

text.text: Your boss wants one great idea by Friday, ideally “for the Shanghai market, since you speak the language”. Last night {friend} told you {friend.his} idea: a dating app for dogs.
Your boss wants one great idea by Friday. Last night, over beers, {friend} told you {friend.his} idea: a dating app for dogs. {Friend.he} hasn't told anyone else.

ok.text: “Sniffr” is a hit. You're promoted. {friend} texts: “we should talk”.

reveal.text: {friend} sees “your” dog app on a billboard. {Friend.he} stops answering your calls.

effects.remember: Got promoted with {friend}'s idea. Didn't mention {friend}.

fail.text: Your boss says it “sounds like something a drunk friend told you”.

choices.label: Pitch your own idea: a loyalty card for pigeons

ok.text: Your boss loves it. The pigeons love it more. Promoted!

effects.remember: Got promoted for a loyalty card for pigeons. The pigeons are very loyal.

fail.text: Your boss asks if everything is okay at home.

choices.label: Ask {friend} to pitch it together with you

ok.text: {friend} agrees. You pitch it as a duo. You both get promoted and hug in front of HR.

effects.remember: Pitched {friend}'s idea together with {friend.him}. Both promoted.

fail.text: {friend} pitches it alone, on Thursday, a day early. {Friend.he} gets your promotion.

effects.remember: Asked {friend} to share {friend.his} idea. {Friend.he} pitched it alone.

choices.label: Calculate that a bridge for dogs would pay for itself in four years

ok.text: Nobody understands the maths, so everybody trusts it. Promoted. The bridge is for small dogs only.

effects.remember: Got promoted for a bridge for dogs. The maths was correct.

choices.label: Spin it out as a startup and offer your boss shares

ok.text: Your boss invests. You're the CEO of something now. Nobody is sure what.

effects.remember: Turned the big pitch into your own company.

title: The Night Shift
text: It's 3 a.m. at {workplace}. You're alone in charge, the coffee machine is broken, and the boss's nephew just walked in covered in glitter and regret.

choices.label: Quietly sort it out and tell nobody

ok.text: You clean him up, call his mum and say nothing. The boss finds out anyway and owes you forever.

effects.remember: Covered for the boss's nephew on the night shift. Got promoted for it.

fail.text: You sort it out. Nobody notices. Not even the boss. Especially not the boss.

choices.label: Take a photo, just in case

ok.text: The photo turns out to be very useful at your next pay review.

secret.text: You have a photo of the boss's nephew

reveal.text: The nephew finds the photo on your phone at the Christmas party. So does everyone else.

effects.remember: Kept a photo of the boss's nephew covered in glitter. For later.

fail.text: The flash goes off. The nephew cries. The boss hears about the photo before the glitter.

ok.text: {friend} arrives in pyjamas with a mop and a bag of crisps. Best night shift ever.

effects.remember: {friend} came to help on your worst night shift.

cast.did: turned up at 3 a.m. in pyjamas

fail.text: {friend} doesn't pick up. In the morning {friend.he} posts a photo of the glitter. {Friend.he} was there. Filming.

choices.label: Treat the glitter like a medical emergency, by the book

ok.text: Your report is so thorough it's used for training. Promoted to {job2}.

effects.remember: Wrote the town's only medical report about glitter.

choices.label: Arrest him for being drunk and sparkly

ok.text: The boss is so impressed by your fairness that you're promoted. The nephew is now very sober.

effects.remember: Arrested the boss's nephew. Got promoted for it.

choices.label: Give him the speech you give Year 6 about choices

ok.text: He cries. He apologises. He becomes a teacher. You're promoted.

effects.remember: Gave the boss's nephew the Year 6 speech. It worked.

text.text: The office Christmas party. Someone made a cake shaped like your pigeon loyalty card. The boss is holding a microphone and looking at you.
The office Christmas party. The boss is holding a microphone and looking for someone to “say a few words”.

ok.text: People cry. The boss cries. You get a pay rise and a hug that lasts too long.

effects.remember: Made the whole office cry with a Christmas speech.

fail.text: You thank your mum, then your ex, then the boss's ex. The music comes back on.

choices.label: Say “I'm just happy to be here” and sit down

ok.text: Everyone respects how humble you are. The boss remembers your name for the first time.

fail.text: You start with “I'm just happy to be here” and then tell everyone about your new watch for nine minutes.

showoff.text: “I'm just happy to be here,” you say, “in my new car, which is outside.” You show them the car. In the rain.

choices.label: Drag {rival} to karaoke for a duet

ok.text: You and {rival} sing a power ballad. It's terrible. Everyone loves it. {rival} almost smiles.

effects.remember: Sang a power ballad with {rival} at the office party.

fail.text: {rival} sings it alone and much better. You hold the microphone stand.
